## Tools

**macOS blackboxd/bro-harness redeploy (stablesign + launchd)**

Redeploy signing now uses the operator's stablesign helper (shell alias `stablesign`) instead of ad-hoc `codesign -f -s -`: it signs with a persistent self-signed codesigning identity from the login keychain, so the designated requirement is stable across binary swaps. Consequences: TCC privacy grants (notably network volumes - an invalidated grant makes daemon-spawned git/fs calls on automounts hang silently, wedging the IndexWriterActor) and launchd's cached LWCR both survive redeploys. Flow: back up prior binary to `.bak` -> cp new binary into ~/.local/bin -> `stablesign ~/.local/bin/blackboxd` -> `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.daystrom.blackbox` (bootout/bootstrap dance only as fallback if kickstart still refuses) -> verify port 7264 responds. If indexing goes quiet after any signing change, check System Settings for a pending TCC consent. Note KeepAlive{SuccessfulExit:false}: a clean exit 0 will NOT be auto-restarted. The daemon links bro-harness/bro-tools in-process, so rebuilding blackboxd captures library-crate changes; rebuild + stablesign the standalone bro-harness bin too for consistency.

**macOS host runs satellites only; corpus daemon lives in the cage**

The corpus daemon runs in the cage (blackbox.daystrom.app); no local blackboxd service exists on this macOS host post-cutover. The com.daystrom.blackbox launchd label is retired and leftover plists on disk are unloaded; nothing serves 127.0.0.1:7264. The host runs only satellites under launchd: collectors (bbox-code-collector, bbox-slack-collector), fleetd, and lane-pool helpers. The stablesign/kickstart redeploy runbook applies only to these locally-deployed sidecar binaries, never to a corpus daemon; corpus changes reach production via the cage image path (submit-bbox-verify.sh gate, submit-bbox-build.sh image, then `scripts/converge.sh --image <tag>` from bbox-cage). Config-dir nuance still applies: Rust dirs::config_dir() resolves to ~/Library/Application Support, so bro fleet may read ~/Library/Application Support/blackbox/fleet.json, while ~/.config/blackbox/ keeps the main config.toml and a mirrored fleet.json; check/update both fleet.json files when changing fleet-local settings unless BLACKBOX_CONFIG is explicitly set.

### macOS redeploy

**stablesign errSecInternalComponent means locked keychain: pause and ask the operator to unlock**

When `stablesign` (b1-stablesign.sh) fails with errSecInternalComponent while re-signing a redeployed binary (blackboxd, bro-harness), the cause is a locked login keychain, not a sandbox or session problem. Do not retry with sandbox tricks, launchctl asuser, or osascript, and do not leave the ad-hoc-signed binary deployed as the outcome. Pause, tell the operator the keychain is locked, ask them to unlock it, then re-run `stablesign <path>` and verify `codesign -dvv` shows Authority=PlanGlobal Stable Codesign before reporting the redeploy done.
